definition: The practice of living together as a sexual or romantic couple outside of legal marriage.
notes: Legally and sociologically coded as implying a sexual relationship; appears frequently in family law, tax, and housing contexts. Not purely a sex act but categorized as such in sexual-behavior research.

definition: The first act of sexual intercourse following a marriage, historically required to render the marriage legally valid.
notes: Still legally relevant in some jurisdictions as grounds for annulment if unconsummated. Register is archaic but not obsolete in legal or religious discourse.

definition: The act of first vaginal penetration, historically framed around rupture of the hymen.
notes: Carries heavy patriarchal and property-of-body framing; modern gynecology rejects the hymen-centric model. Term has largely been displaced by 'loss of virginity' or 'first penetrative sex' in contemporary usage.

definition: A contraceptive method in which the penis is withdrawn from the vagina before ejaculation.
notes: Colloquially 'pulling out'. Latin phrase used in clinical and public-health writing. Efficacy as contraception is widely debated due to pre-ejaculate sperm.

definition: Sexual arousal and gratification obtained through self-stimulation or self-directed erotic fantasy.
notes: Broader than masturbation — encompasses fantasy, body-wide stimulation, and non-genital self-arousal. Term has Freudian clinical lineage; rarely used outside academic or psychoanalytic writing.

definition: Sexual intercourse; an archaic formal term for coitus.
notes: Largely confined to legal briefs, historical texts, and satirical prose today. The word 'congress' (coming together) is the operative metaphor.

definition: Sexual intercourse; historically the statutory legal phrase used in criminal codes for rape and unlawful sex with a minor.
notes: 'Carnal' (from Latin caro, flesh) adds a moral/bodily-sin connotation absent from clinical 'intercourse'. Primarily encountered today in legal history and biblical commentary.

definition: A legal and religious term historically encompassing anal intercourse, oral sex, or bestiality, derived from the biblical city of Sodom.
notes: U.S. sodomy laws struck down by Lawrence v. Texas (2003). Contemporary colloquial usage has narrowed to anal intercourse. The term carries irreducible moral-religious charge regardless of legal context.

definition: Sexual contact or intercourse between a human and a non-human animal.
notes: Refers to the act; distinguished from zoophilia (the attraction). Illegal in most jurisdictions. Widely recognized term from legal reporting and taboo-topic discourse.

definition: A paraphilia characterized by sexual attraction to non-human animals as the primary or preferred erotic focus.
notes: Foregrounds attraction and identity rather than behavior (cf. bestiality). Used in forensic psychiatry and, self-referentially, by zoophile communities online. Very low public recognition of this specific term.

definition: Sexual attraction to or sexual acts performed with a human corpse.
notes: Illegal in most jurisdictions. Clinical literature distinguishes exclusive, preferential, and situational subtypes. Term is broadly recognized from crime reporting, horror fiction, and tabloid media.

definition: Any persistent pattern of sexual arousal centered on atypical objects, situations, or individuals, as defined in the DSM-5 classification system.
notes: DSM-5 distinguishes paraphilia (atypical but not inherently disordered) from paraphilic disorder (causing distress or harm to self or others). 'Fetish' is the lay equivalent but is narrower. Very low public recognition of the clinical phrase.

definition: Sexual intercourse involving penetration of the vagina by the penis; the precise clinical descriptor used in public health and epidemiological research.
notes: Abbreviated PVI in research literature. Adoption of this term reflects need to distinguish among sexual act types for STI transmission risk stratification.

definition: The act of receiving anal penetration during sexual intercourse; the clinical descriptor for the 'bottom' role.
notes: Abbreviated RAI in HIV/STI research. Epidemiologically significant as the highest-risk position for HIV transmission per act. The colloquial equivalent 'bottoming' carries gay male cultural connotations absent from the clinical phrase.

definition: The act of penetrating a partner anally during sexual intercourse; the clinical descriptor for the 'top' role.
notes: Abbreviated IAI in HIV/STI research. Lower but non-negligible HIV transmission risk compared to RAI. As with RAI, the colloquial 'topping' carries gay male cultural connotations not embedded in the clinical phrase.

definition: Sexual stimulation of the perineum, the region of skin and tissue between the genitals and the anus.
notes: The perineum is colloquially called the 'taint', 'gooch', 'grundle', or 'chode' (regional variation). Appears in sex therapy and pelvic floor physical therapy literature; extremely low general public recognition of the clinical phrase.

definition: Sexual stimulation of the prostate gland, typically via the rectum, for pleasure or therapeutic purposes.
notes: Colloquially called 'P-spot' stimulation; also 'milking' in kink contexts. Mainstream awareness has increased through sex-positive media and prostate health campaigns aimed at cis men.

definition: Direct or indirect manual, oral, or mechanical stimulation of the clitoris for sexual arousal and pleasure.
notes: Central mechanism of orgasm for the majority of vulva-owners; increasingly prominent in mainstream sex education since the 2010s. 'Clitoral' sits near the boundary of clinical and plain English.

definition: Stimulation of the anterior wall of the vagina at the presumed location of the G-spot, associated with heightened arousal and sometimes ejaculation.
notes: Named after Ernst Gräfenberg (1950). Anatomical existence contested in peer-reviewed literature; widely accepted in popular discourse. Public awareness peaked roughly 2005–2015 with wave of lifestyle-magazine coverage.

definition: The intentional restriction of oxygen supply to the brain during sexual activity to intensify arousal or orgasm.
notes: Colloquially 'breath play' or 'choking'. Associated with accidental deaths including autoerotic asphyxiation cases (Michael Hutchence 1997, David Carradine 2009), which drove mainstream awareness spikes. 'Choking' as consensual kink has been widely discussed in mainstream media since ~2018.

definition: A paraphilia characterized by sexual arousal specifically from oxygen deprivation, whether self-inflicted or partner-inflicted.
notes: Subcategory of paraphilia used in forensic psychiatry and sexology literature. Virtually unknown outside clinical audiences; 'erotic asphyxiation' is the public-facing equivalent. Some literature also uses 'hypoxyphilia'.

definition: The sexual practice of inserting a fully folded hand, and sometimes part of the forearm, into the vagina or rectum.
notes: The term functions as its own clinical-adjacent common name; no more formal alternative is in wide use. Practiced in heterosexual, lesbian, and gay male communities. Requires progressive dilation and lubrication; closely associated with the practice listed as 'stretching'.

definition: The gradual dilation of the vaginal or rectal opening using progressively larger objects, practiced in sex therapy or as a kink end in itself.
notes: Heavily polysemous — recognition rate is conditional on sexual context being established. Clinical equivalent is 'progressive vaginal/rectal dilation'. In kink communities, also called 'gaping' when referring to the resulting state rather than the process. Recognition figure reflects sexual-context usage only.

definition: To have sexual intercourse; the most common and most vulgar English verb for the sex act.
notes: One of the most versatile words in English — verb, noun, interjection, and intensifier — with many uses fully detached from sexual meaning. Etymology uncertain; attested in English from at least the early 16th century. The crude connotations are irreducible even when used neutrally by speakers; 'have sex' captures the act but loses all register charge.

definition: To have sexual intercourse; a mildly crude slang verb less transgressive than 'fuck'.
notes: Operates on a mechanical metaphor of rotary penetration, shared with 'nail', 'drill', and 'bang'. Also means to cheat or defraud ('screw over'), which somewhat dilutes the sexual salience. Slightly dated as sexual slang; peak usage estimated mid-to-late 20th century.
